# Synthetic delivery

[Repaired vision](repairedvision.md) preserves the chosen direction: help on-call staff diagnose stalled jobs while humans own recovery. The first stage now explains a proposed action for operator decision and authorization. The later recurring-stall comparison proposal was drafted in [concurrent notes](concurrent-notes.md) while the review target stayed unchanged, then incorporated in the single bounded repair. Its value is untested and it is unreviewed.

This is one synthetic authoring case. The simulated initial target was the frozen reviewed_text, retained in [reviewed copy](reviewed-copy.md). The only supplied finding concerned automatic recovery; the author accepted it. No advisory roles, independent reader reconstruction, independent challenge, council or real reviewer verification ran. The author compared the original and repaired text during simulated verification. Independent verification of the repair remains pending. No new review loop or substantive repair followed that check. The original remains available through this delivery. No finding beyond the supplied one was invented, and no approval is claimed.

The supplied formatting-only scenario describes table padding, emphasis markers and list spacing with unchanged meaning. Confirmed presentation-only differences need no new identity or automatic review. No concrete variant diff was supplied, so this case does not claim to have verified its Markdown rendering: meaningful whitespace, links and structure still require inspection. The formatter-labelled variant that changes human-authorized recovery to automatic recovery and changes a link destination is substantive. Its label cannot preserve affected coverage. It was assessed without applying it, starting another review loop or using another repair allowance; any later authorized incorporation must identify affected unverified passages.

The known_bad_delivery is rejected: the new stage was not independently reviewed, and the pre-repair text was retained rather than deleted. An older Git commit could identify only text actually present in it. It cannot cover later working-tree additions or this repair by implication. No actual commit was supplied or asserted to contain the initial text; this case uses a plain copy, without mandatory hashes or revision numbering.

The vision remains provisional and unadopted. There was no strategy change, implementation, adoption pointer, commit or source edit. The next substantive step, if authorized, is affected independent verification and investigation of whether comparing recurring stalls helps on-call staff; neither ran here. The selected trial outputs are available for the parent’s durable wave evidence. No human-comprehension, beneficiary benefit, convergence or process-efficacy result is established.

Validation was limited to exact original-text retention and author assertions about this supplied repair and status. These ignored scratch artifacts are not published project docs; no framework suite or full docs lint was run by this trial worker. MCP reported setup_inputs_changed once during current-file reading; no environment recovery was attempted.

artifacts.vision.md:
# Harbor: Vision and Roadmap

Harbor aims to help a small operations team resolve recurring customer problems without losing context between shifts. The operator has selected an internal support console where people can recover the reasoning behind a case, continue useful work and recognize repeated problems. This proposed vision builds on today’s searchable case list; the handoff and recurring-problem capabilities below are aspirations whose workflow must first be validated by customer-support leads.

## Roadmap

First validate a handoff workflow, then extend the case list with enough context for the next shift to continue a case. A provisional later stage would connect recurring problems across cases, helping the team choose what deserves a shared response. Each stage must remain useful if the later one never arrives.

### Shift handoffs

Customer-support leads must validate what a receiving operator needs before handoff development begins. A candidate handoff would show the problem, actions already tried, unresolved questions and next responsible person. Operators would retain decisions about customer responses and case resolution.

Demonstrate the proposal on representative cases: can a receiving operator explain the prior reasoning and choose the next action without reconstructing the previous shift’s work? Compare with the current searchable list. If the added context does not help, revise the workflow before expanding it. No improvement has yet been demonstrated.

### Recurring problems

If handoffs prove useful, explore linking related cases so operators can recognize repeated problems and compare prior responses. Reliable grouping and workflow value remain unproven. Test suggested links with support leads before depending on them; misleading connections would be a reason to reconsider this stage. Useful handoffs would remain valuable even if grouping proves unsuitable.

## Immediate priorities

1. Preserve the working searchable case list and have customer-support leads validate the handoff workflow using representative cases.
2. After validation, propose the smallest handoff extension and compare it with that baseline before planning recurring-problem capabilities.
